subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution followed by failed delivery become a first-class `warning` run status, or should cron keep `status=ok` and surface the delivery failure through delivery fields and UI presentation?
rationale: Both models are plausible and already represented by open PRs, but the choice changes persisted status, Gateway schema, Control UI rendering, backoff, and external consumer semantics.

options.title: Use ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Land the narrower execution/delivery split and make UI and operators read `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics for undelivered successful runs.

options.title: Add first-class warning
options.body: Adopt the broader `warning` status only after updating storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and compatibility proof across clients.

options.title: Keep delivery failures as errors
options.body: Reject the split for now so post-run delivery failures continue to drive `status=error`, backoff, and failure alerts.

recommendation.title: Use ok plus delivery fields
recommendation.body: Land the narrower execution/delivery split and make UI and operators read `deliveryStatus`, `lastDeliveryError`, and diagnostics for undelivered successful runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron feature/status history makes this the strongest available owner for the cross-surface product/API choice.
